item.title: Expeditions
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description: Some ideas can only be understood by leaving the desk. Expeditions is the record of that — the trips taken not for leisure but for evidence: the site visit, the interview in a language you’re only half-fluent in, the data collected standing in the rain because the instrument couldn’t wait for better weather. This is where the mess of real fieldwork gets written down before it’s sanded into a tidy report somewhere else — the wrong turns, the local who explained more in five minutes than the literature did in five papers, the moment a hypothesis quietly died on contact with reality. If you’ve ever come back from a trip with more questions than you left with, you already know the feeling this section is built around.

item.title: Featured Partners
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description: The honest one, if only because it says what it is right in the name. Featured Partners is clearly marked space for paid or collaborative content — a boundary drawn on purpose so the rest of the site doesn’t have to wonder where the line is. Done well, it’s a place where sponsorship and genuine usefulness aren’t at odds; done badly, it’s the section readers learn to skip. Naming it plainly, rather than dressing it up as something else, is what keeps the trust intact everywhere else.

item.title: Narratives
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description: The section without a hook, because it doesn’t need one — this is just the writing. Personal essays, short fiction, the pieces that don’t fit a beat or a format and exist purely because something needed to be said in sentence form. Narratives is less a category than a home base: the place other sections borrow their tone from when they’re at their best. It asks the most of both writer and reader, and it’s usually where the writer would point first if asked what they’re actually proud of.

item.title: Punditry & Parody
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description: Two moods sharing one roof. Punditry is the straight take — an actual argument, made in good faith, about the state of things. Parody is what happens when the straight take isn’t enough, when the news has already outpaced satire and the only honest response left is to exaggerate it further. Together they let a writer be serious and ridiculous in the same week, sometimes the same piece, without pretending those are contradictions. This is the section with the most risk in it — the one likeliest to make someone close the tab — and also, often, the most alive.

item.title: Respawn
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description: The name says it plainly: you die, you come back, you try again — and somewhere in that loop is the whole appeal of games as a subject worth writing about. Respawn isn’t a scoreboard or a review column; it’s closer to a journal kept between sessions, tracking not just what happened in the game but what it stirred up outside of it. A boss fight that mirrored a bad week. A slow, wandering open world that taught patience nobody asked for. The pleasure of a genre you’re embarrassed to admit you love. This section treats games as worth the same reflective attention as a book or a film — maybe more, since you actually had to survive them.

item.title: The Guestbook
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description: Every project eventually outgrows a single voice, and The Guestbook is the acknowledgment of that. It’s a room set aside for other people’s stories — submitted, gathered, transcribed, sometimes lightly polished but never rewritten past recognition. The name does double duty: a guestbook is what strangers sign on their way through, and also what a house keeps to remember who’s been in it. This section is quieter than the others because it isn’t the writer’s job to be the loudest voice in it — just the one holding the door.

item.title: Two Fathers
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description:
Two Fathers

A confession, not a story — because I have nothing left to lose.

I have two fathers. One no longer speaks to me. The other I carry in my pocket.

The second one is a pink tablet, small as a chickpea, with two letters stamped into its face. On the street it goes by many names — guti, maal — but the most common one will make your skin crawl. Baba. Father. Yes: across this country, hundreds of thousands of boys call that pink thing Baba. It took me twenty-four years to understand why. Like a father, it holds you when you fall. It reassures you. And one day you look up and realize you are nothing without it.

item.title: Unfiltered
item.author: yum0@limbomail.com (Servus Dei Custoditus)
item.description: No thesis, no research, no performance — just the low-stakes overflow of a mind that thinks in public. Unfiltered is where a bad night’s sleep, a strong opinion about a sandwich, or a half-formed thought that never became an essay gets to exist without needing to justify itself. It’s the section most readers will feel closest to, precisely because it asks the least of them, and it’s often the one a writer needs most, if only to prove the other sections aren’t the whole story.
